acceptanceReadbacks.ssot: CloudIdentityAuthorization — a live session, audience, action and exact resource on every privileged call.
acceptanceReadbacks.implementation: the owner asks the live authority and the BFF guards every route with session, CSRF, same-origin and idempotency.
acceptanceReadbacks.case: A platform administrator is admitted; a tenant administrator, a member attempting an administrator action and an anonymous caller are refused; a refusal arrives as a decision rather than an outage.

proven: The running Console BFF process serves the catalog surface: the acceptance check builds and starts the actual product binary and reaches the routes through its own configuration, not a test-assembled handler.
A real platform administrator creates approved compute and storage plans and retires one through that process, and the owner's own rows are the authority for the readback.
A money-bearing price policy version round-trips the contract's property spelling and decimal-string amount in both directions, and the owner row carries the amount.
A tenant administrator and a member attempting an administrator action are refused, an anonymous caller is refused, and a refusal leaves no row behind.
A member reads the customer catalog list and is refused the administrator policy surface.
Retiring a plan changes the owner's availability projection, and pricing the retired pair is refused at the owner boundary.
A CloudIdentity refusal reaches the owner as PermissionDenied, an unusable session as Unauthenticated, and only a genuine authority failure as Unavailable; neither refusal writes anything.
Idempotent replay returns the original row, a conflicting body is refused with 409, and a lost-response retry converges on the original row.
The owner's runtime cannot read another owner's data, and this branch carries no identity, contract or public-guard code of its own.
The full local gate passes at zero PostgreSQL skips on the frozen revision with a clean tracked worktree throughout.
notProven: Quoting does not exist. CreateQuote, GetQuote and the Workspace-facing AcceptQuote are unimplemented, so nothing prices a deploy, resize or renew request, and no Local deployment loop exists. Catalog availability is not quoting.
No Workspace subscription, original order, resource intent or provider resource was created or verified, and Fabric's resource reference and authoritative readback are untouched by this slice.

The Ledger DomainInbox still accepts only tenant-scoped build and capability producers, so the platform-scoped catalog.policy_changed.v1 delivery stays pending. The producer records and retries it; the consumer extension is Ledger's write set and the event is not claimed end to end.

The platform-administrator-versus-member read of the customer plan list remains an unresolved contract decision point: the contract grants listComputePlans/listStoragePlans to member, a platform administrator has no tenant, and 04 lists listComputePlans as an administrator page source. Neither side was changed; the check uses a member for the customer read and the administrator for the administrator surface.
No Candidate, Product Release, deployment or Instance qualification was performed, and no production endpoint, database or service was accessed.

The three SIGKILLed gate attempts below mean the recorded pass is the fourth attempt on this revision; the host was under heavy memory pressure from other lanes' concurrent browser suites, not from this change.
